question: List every album together with its artist. Return album ID, album title, and artist name.

question: List tracks from the album Big Ones. Return track ID, track name, duration in milliseconds, and unit price.

question: Show every track classified as Rock. Return track ID and track name.

question: Which tracks use the MPEG audio file media type? Return track ID and track name.

question: List the tracks in playlist ID 1, named Music. Return track ID and track name.
gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name FROM playlists p JOIN playlist_track pt ON pt.playlist_id = p.playlist_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = pt.track_id WHERE p.playlist_id = 1 AND p.name = 'Music' ORDER BY t.name, t.track_id

question: Show each customer with the name of their support representative. Return customer ID, first name, last name, support representative first name, and support representative last name.

question: List invoices for the customer named Frank Ralston. Return invoice ID, invoice date, billing country, and invoice total.

question: How many albums has each artist recorded? Return artist ID, artist name, and album count.
gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, COUNT(al.album_id) AS album_count FROM artists ar LEFT JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name ORDER BY album_count DESC, ar.name, ar.artist_id

question: Which artist has recorded the most albums? Return artist ID, artist name, and album count. If artists are tied, choose alphabetically by artist name and then by artist ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, COUNT(al.album_id) AS album_count FROM artists ar LEFT JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name ORDER BY album_count DESC, ar.name, ar.artist_id LIMIT 1

question: How many tracks are on each album? Return album ID, album title, and track count.
gold_sql: SELECT al.album_id, al.title, COUNT(t.track_id) AS track_count FROM albums al LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id GROUP BY al.album_id, al.title ORDER BY track_count DESC, al.title, al.album_id

question: Which album contains the most tracks? Return album ID, album title, and track count. If albums are tied, choose alphabetically by album title and then by album ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT al.album_id, al.title, COUNT(t.track_id) AS track_count FROM albums al LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id GROUP BY al.album_id, al.title ORDER BY track_count DESC, al.title, al.album_id LIMIT 1

question: How many tracks belong to each genre? Return genre ID, genre name, and track count.
gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, COUNT(t.track_id) AS track_count FROM genres g LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY track_count DESC, g.name, g.genre_id

question: Which genre has the most catalogue tracks? Return genre ID, genre name, and track count. If genres are tied, choose alphabetically by genre name and then by genre ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, COUNT(t.track_id) AS track_count FROM genres g LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY track_count DESC, g.name, g.genre_id LIMIT 1

question: What is the average track duration for each genre, in minutes? Return genre ID, genre name, and average duration in minutes.
gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, AVG(t.milliseconds) / 60000.0 AS average_minutes FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY average_minutes DESC, g.name, g.genre_id

question: Which genre has the longest average track duration? Return genre ID, genre name, and average duration in minutes. If genres are tied, choose alphabetically by genre name and then by genre ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, AVG(t.milliseconds) / 60000.0 AS average_minutes FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY average_minutes DESC, g.name, g.genre_id LIMIT 1

question: How many tracks use each media type? Return media type ID, media type name, and track count.
gold_sql: SELECT mt.media_type_id, mt.name, COUNT(t.track_id) AS track_count FROM media_types mt LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.media_type_id = mt.media_type_id GROUP BY mt.media_type_id, mt.name ORDER BY track_count DESC, mt.name, mt.media_type_id

question: How many tracks are included in each playlist? Return playlist ID, playlist name, and track count.
gold_sql: SELECT p.playlist_id, p.name, COUNT(pt.track_id) AS track_count FROM playlists p LEFT JOIN playlist_track pt ON pt.playlist_id = p.playlist_id GROUP BY p.playlist_id, p.name ORDER BY track_count DESC, p.name, p.playlist_id

question: Which playlist contains the most tracks? Return playlist ID, playlist name, and track count. If playlists are tied, choose alphabetically by playlist name and then by playlist ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT p.playlist_id, p.name, COUNT(pt.track_id) AS track_count FROM playlists p LEFT JOIN playlist_track pt ON pt.playlist_id = p.playlist_id GROUP BY p.playlist_id, p.name ORDER BY track_count DESC, p.name, p.playlist_id LIMIT 1

question: How much invoice revenue is associated with each customer? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and invoice revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COALESCE(SUM(i.total), 0) AS invoice_revenue FROM customers c LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY invoice_revenue DESC, c.customer_id

question: Which customer has the highest total invoice value? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and total invoice revenue. If customers are tied, choose by customer ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(i.total) AS invoice_revenue FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY invoice_revenue DESC, c.customer_id LIMIT 1

question: How many orders has each customer placed? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and order count.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT i.invoice_id) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.customer_id

question: Which customers have placed at least seven orders? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and order count.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT i.invoice_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT i.invoice_id) >= 7 ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.customer_id

question: What is total invoice revenue by billing country?
gold_sql: SELECT billing_country, SUM(total) AS invoice_revenue FROM invoices GROUP BY billing_country ORDER BY invoice_revenue DESC, billing_country

question: Which billing country generated the most invoice revenue? Return billing country and invoice revenue. If countries are tied, choose alphabetically by billing country.
gold_sql: SELECT billing_country, SUM(total) AS invoice_revenue FROM invoices GROUP BY billing_country ORDER BY invoice_revenue DESC, billing_country LIMIT 1

question: What is the average invoice total in each billing country?
gold_sql: SELECT billing_country, AVG(total) AS average_invoice_total FROM invoices GROUP BY billing_country ORDER BY average_invoice_total DESC, billing_country

question: How many distinct customers were billed in each country?

question: Show total invoice revenue for each calendar year.

question: Show total invoice revenue for each month in 2012.
gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date) AS invoice_month, SUM(total) AS invoice_revenue FROM invoices WHERE invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date) ORDER BY invoice_month

question: How many invoices were issued in each month of 2011?
gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date) AS invoice_month, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM invoices WHERE invoice_date >= DATE '2011-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2012-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date) ORDER BY invoice_month

question: Compare total invoice revenue in 2011 and 2012.
gold_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) AS invoice_year, SUM(total) AS invoice_revenue FROM invoices WHERE invoice_date >= DATE '2011-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) ORDER BY invoice_year

question: What is the total realised revenue from invoice line items?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(unit_price * quantity) AS realised_revenue FROM invoice_items

question: How many units were sold in total?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(quantity) AS units_sold FROM invoice_items

question: How many distinct tracks have ever been sold?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT track_id) AS sold_track_count FROM invoice_items

question: Return the ten best-selling tracks by units sold, including track ID, name, and units sold. Order them by units sold in descending order, and break ties alphabetically by track name and then by track ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name, SUM(ii.quantity) AS units_sold FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id GROUP BY t.track_id, t.name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, t.name, t.track_id LIMIT 10

question: Return the ten highest-revenue tracks, including track ID, name, and realised revenue. Order them by revenue in descending order, and break ties alphabetically by track name and then by track ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id GROUP BY t.track_id, t.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, t.name, t.track_id LIMIT 10

question: Which tracks have never been sold? Return track ID and track name.
gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name FROM tracks t LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id WHERE ii.track_id IS NULL ORDER BY t.name, t.track_id

question: How many units were sold for each genre? Return genre ID, genre name, and units sold.
gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, SUM(ii.quantity) AS units_sold FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, g.name, g.genre_id

question: Which genre generated the most realised revenue? Return genre ID, genre name, and realised revenue. If genres are tied, choose alphabetically by genre name and then by genre ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, g.name, g.genre_id LIMIT 1

question: What was realised revenue by genre in 2012? Return genre ID, genre name, and revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE i.invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND i.invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, g.name, g.genre_id

question: How much realised revenue did each album generate? Return album ID, album title, and revenue.

question: How many customers are assigned to each support representative? Return employee ID, first name, last name, and customer count.

question: What total invoice value is associated with each support representative's customers? Return employee ID, first name, last name, and invoice revenue.

question: Show each employee together with their manager's name. Return employee ID, first name, last name, manager first name, and manager last name.
gold_sql: SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, m.first_name AS manager_first_name, m.last_name AS manager_last_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.reports_to ORDER BY e.employee_id

question: How many direct reports does each employee have? Return employee ID, first name, last name, and direct-report count.

question: Which genres contain more than 100 catalogue tracks? Return genre ID, genre name, and track count.

question: Which artists have more than five albums? Return artist ID, artist name, and album count.

question: For each customer country, how many customers have a company recorded and how many do not?

question: What is the average catalogue price by genre? Return genre ID, genre name, and average track price.

question: What is the total duration in hours of the tracks on each album? Return album ID, album title, and total duration in hours.

question: Which artist has the greatest total catalogue duration? Return artist ID, artist name, and total duration in hours. If artists are tied, choose alphabetically by artist name and then by artist ID in ascending order.

question: Which tracks appear in more than one playlist? Return track ID, track name, and playlist count.

question: How many distinct tracks occur in any playlist?

question: Which catalogue tracks do not occur in any playlist? Return track ID and track name.

question: For each customer, show their country and every distinct country where their invoices were billed. Return customer ID, first name, last name, customer country, and billing country.

question: Which invoices were billed to a different country from the customer's recorded country? Return invoice ID, customer ID, customer country, billing country, invoice date, and invoice total.
gold_sql: SELECT i.invoice_id, c.customer_id, c.country AS customer_country, i.billing_country, i.invoice_date, i.total FROM invoices i JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id WHERE i.billing_country <> c.country ORDER BY i.invoice_date, i.invoice_id

question: Which customers made a purchase in 2013? Return customer ID, first name, and last name.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE i.invoice_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND i.invoice_date < DATE '2014-01-01' ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name, c.customer_id

question: How many distinct customers purchased in each year?
gold_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) AS invoice_year, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customer_count FROM invoices GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) ORDER BY invoice_year

question: Which customers have never placed an order? Return customer ID, first name, and last name.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE i.customer_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name, c.customer_id

question: Which artists have no albums in the catalogue? Return artist ID and artist name.
gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name FROM artists ar LEFT JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id WHERE al.artist_id IS NULL ORDER BY ar.name, ar.artist_id

question: Calculate realised revenue for every artist. Return artist ID, artist name, and revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN albums al ON al.album_id = t.album_id JOIN artists ar ON ar.artist_id = al.artist_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, ar.name, ar.artist_id

question: Rank artists by total units sold. Return artist ID, artist name, and units sold, ordered by units sold in descending order. Break ties alphabetically by artist name and then by artist ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, SUM(ii.quantity) AS units_sold FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN albums al ON al.album_id = t.album_id JOIN artists ar ON ar.artist_id = al.artist_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, ar.name, ar.artist_id

question: Which artist generated the most realised revenue during 2012? Return artist ID, artist name, and realised revenue. If artists are tied, choose alphabetically by artist name and then by artist ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN albums al ON al.album_id = t.album_id JOIN artists ar ON ar.artist_id = al.artist_id WHERE i.invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND i.invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, ar.name, ar.artist_id LIMIT 1

question: Show units sold and realised revenue for every album. Return album ID, album title, units sold, and revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT al.album_id, al.title, SUM(ii.quantity) AS units_sold, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN albums al ON al.album_id = t.album_id GROUP BY al.album_id, al.title ORDER BY revenue DESC, al.title, al.album_id

question: List each customer and every genre they have purchased. Return customer ID, first name, last name, genre ID, and genre name.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, g.genre_id, g.name AS genre_name FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id ORDER BY c.customer_id, g.name, g.genre_id

question: Which customers bought at least one Rock track? Return customer ID, first name, and last name.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE g.name = 'Rock' ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name, c.customer_id

question: How many distinct genres has each customer purchased? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and genre count.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.genre_id) AS genre_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY genre_count DESC, c.customer_id

question: Which customers have purchased tracks from at least ten distinct genres? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and genre count.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.genre_id) AS genre_count FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.genre_id) >= 10 ORDER BY genre_count DESC, c.customer_id

question: Show realised revenue by billing country and genre. Return billing country, genre ID, genre name, and revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT i.billing_country, g.genre_id, g.name AS genre_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id GROUP BY i.billing_country, g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY i.billing_country, revenue DESC, g.name, g.genre_id

question: For each billing country, identify the genre with the highest realised revenue. Return billing country, genre ID, genre name, and revenue.
gold_sql: WITH genre_revenue AS (SELECT i.billing_country, g.genre_id, g.name AS genre_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id GROUP BY i.billing_country, g.genre_id, g.name), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY billing_country ORDER BY revenue DESC, genre_name, genre_id) AS rn FROM genre_revenue) SELECT billing_country, genre_id, genre_name, revenue FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY billing_country

question: Find the highest-spending customer in each customer country using total invoice value. Return country, customer ID, first name, last name, and revenue.
gold_sql: WITH customer_revenue AS (SELECT c.country, c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(i.total) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.country, c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY revenue DESC, customer_id) AS rn FROM customer_revenue) SELECT country, customer_id, first_name, last_name, revenue FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY country

question: Show realised line-item revenue for every month.
gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', i.invoice_date) AS invoice_month, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', i.invoice_date) ORDER BY invoice_month

question: For each year, show invoice revenue and the change from the previous year.
gold_sql: WITH yearly AS (SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) AS invoice_year, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM invoices GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date)) SELECT invoice_year, revenue, revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY invoice_year) AS change_from_previous_year FROM yearly ORDER BY invoice_year

question: For each customer, show the number of days between their first and last invoice. Return customer ID, first name, last name, and number of days.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, DATE_DIFF('day', MIN(i.invoice_date), MAX(i.invoice_date)) AS customer_span_days FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY customer_span_days DESC, c.customer_id

question: Show each customer's first invoice, including its date and total. Return customer ID, first name, last name, invoice ID, invoice date, and invoice total.
gold_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT i.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.customer_id ORDER BY i.invoice_date, i.invoice_id) AS rn FROM invoices i) SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, r.invoice_id, r.invoice_date, r.total FROM customers c JOIN ranked r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id AND r.rn = 1 ORDER BY c.customer_id

question: Show each customer's most recent invoice, including its date and total. Return customer ID, first name, last name, invoice ID, invoice date, and invoice total.
gold_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT i.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.customer_id ORDER BY i.invoice_date DESC, i.invoice_id DESC) AS rn FROM invoices i) SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, r.invoice_id, r.invoice_date, r.total FROM customers c JOIN ranked r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id AND r.rn = 1 ORDER BY c.customer_id

question: Which invoices have a total greater than the overall average invoice total? Return invoice ID, customer ID, invoice date, and invoice total.
gold_sql: SELECT invoice_id, customer_id, invoice_date, total FROM invoices WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM invoices) ORDER BY total DESC, invoice_id

question: Which albums have no tracks that were ever sold? Return album ID and album title.
gold_sql: SELECT al.album_id, al.title FROM albums al WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tracks t JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id WHERE t.album_id = al.album_id) ORDER BY al.title, al.album_id

question: Which artists have never had any track sold? Return artist ID and artist name.
gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name FROM artists ar WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM albums al JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id WHERE al.artist_id = ar.artist_id) ORDER BY ar.name, ar.artist_id

question: Which tracks have both been sold and included in at least one playlist? Return track ID and track name.
gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name FROM tracks t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoice_items ii WHERE ii.track_id = t.track_id) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM playlist_track pt WHERE pt.track_id = t.track_id) ORDER BY t.name, t.track_id

question: What is the average number of line items per invoice?
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(line_count) AS average_line_items FROM (SELECT invoice_id, COUNT(*) AS line_count FROM invoice_items GROUP BY invoice_id) invoice_lines

question: Which customers have a total invoice value above the average customer total? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and revenue.
gold_sql: WITH customer_totals AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(i.total) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name) SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, revenue FROM customer_totals WHERE revenue > (SELECT AVG(revenue) FROM customer_totals) ORDER BY revenue DESC, customer_id

question: Which tracks generated more revenue than the average revenue among sold tracks? Return track ID, track name, and revenue.
gold_sql: WITH track_revenue AS (SELECT t.track_id, t.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM tracks t JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY t.track_id, t.name) SELECT track_id, name, revenue FROM track_revenue WHERE revenue > (SELECT AVG(revenue) FROM track_revenue) ORDER BY revenue DESC, name, track_id

question: For each artist, compare catalogue track count with the number of distinct tracks sold. Return artist ID, artist name, catalogue track count, and distinct sold-track count.
gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.track_id) AS catalogue_tracks, COUNT(DISTINCT ii.track_id) AS sold_tracks FROM artists ar LEFT JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name ORDER BY ar.name, ar.artist_id

question: For each customer with at least two invoices, what was their longest gap in days between consecutive invoices? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and longest gap in days.
gold_sql: WITH dated_invoices AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, i.invoice_id, i.invoice_date, LAG(i.invoice_date) OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_id ORDER BY i.invoice_date, i.invoice_id) AS previous_invoice_date FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id), invoice_gaps AS (SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, date_diff('day', previous_invoice_date, invoice_date) AS gap_days FROM dated_invoices WHERE previous_invoice_date IS NOT NULL) SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, MAX(gap_days) AS longest_gap_days FROM invoice_gaps GROUP BY customer_id, first_name, last_name ORDER BY longest_gap_days DESC, customer_id

question: Which albums were purchased in at least five distinct billing countries? Return album ID, album title, billing-country count, and realised revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT al.album_id, al.title, COUNT(DISTINCT i.billing_country) AS billing_country_count, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM albums al JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_id = ii.invoice_id GROUP BY al.album_id, al.title HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT i.billing_country) >= 5 ORDER BY billing_country_count DESC, revenue DESC, al.album_id

question: Return the 20 pairs of tracks purchased together on the same invoice most often. Within each pair, use the lower track ID as the first track and the higher track ID as the second. Return first track ID, first track name, second track ID, second track name, and the number of invoices containing the pair. Order by that invoice count in descending order, and break ties by first track ID and then second track ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT t1.track_id AS track_1_id, t1.name AS track_1_name, t2.track_id AS track_2_id, t2.name AS track_2_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ii1.invoice_id) AS invoices_together FROM invoice_items ii1 JOIN invoice_items ii2 ON ii2.invoice_id = ii1.invoice_id AND ii1.track_id < ii2.track_id JOIN tracks t1 ON t1.track_id = ii1.track_id JOIN tracks t2 ON t2.track_id = ii2.track_id GROUP BY t1.track_id, t1.name, t2.track_id, t2.name ORDER BY invoices_together DESC, track_1_id, track_2_id LIMIT 20

question: How many distinct genres are represented in each playlist? Return playlist ID, playlist name, and genre count.
gold_sql: SELECT p.playlist_id, p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.genre_id) AS genre_count FROM playlists p JOIN playlist_track pt ON pt.playlist_id = p.playlist_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = pt.track_id GROUP BY p.playlist_id, p.name ORDER BY genre_count DESC, p.name, p.playlist_id

question: What is the most represented genre in each playlist by track count? Return playlist ID, playlist name, genre ID, genre name, and track count.
gold_sql: WITH genre_counts AS (SELECT p.playlist_id, p.name AS playlist_name, g.genre_id, g.name AS genre_name, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM playlists p JOIN playlist_track pt ON pt.playlist_id = p.playlist_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = pt.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id GROUP BY p.playlist_id, p.name, g.genre_id, g.name), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY playlist_id ORDER BY track_count DESC, genre_name, genre_id) AS rn FROM genre_counts) SELECT playlist_id, playlist_name, genre_id, genre_name, track_count FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY playlist_name, playlist_id

question: For each media type, return media type ID, media type name, units sold, and realised revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT mt.media_type_id, mt.name, SUM(ii.quantity) AS units_sold, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN media_types mt ON mt.media_type_id = t.media_type_id GROUP BY mt.media_type_id, mt.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, mt.name, mt.media_type_id

question: Show realised revenue by composer, grouping missing composers as Unknown.
gold_sql: SELECT COALESCE(t.composer, 'Unknown') AS composer, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id GROUP BY COALESCE(t.composer, 'Unknown') ORDER BY revenue DESC, composer

question: How much realised revenue came from tracks without composer information?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id WHERE t.composer IS NULL

question: Rank support representatives by realised line-item revenue from their customers. Return employee ID, first name, last name, and realised revenue, ordered by revenue in descending order. Break ties by employee ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM employees e JOIN customers c ON c.support_rep_id = e.employee_id JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name ORDER BY revenue DESC, e.employee_id

question: Which support representative's customers generated the most realised revenue in 2012? Return employee ID, first name, last name, and realised revenue. If representatives are tied, choose by employee ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM employees e JOIN customers c ON c.support_rep_id = e.employee_id JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id WHERE i.invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND i.invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name ORDER BY revenue DESC, e.employee_id LIMIT 1

question: For each manager, return their employee ID, first name, last name, and the number of customers assigned to their direct-report employees.
gold_sql: SELECT m.employee_id, m.first_name, m.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM employees m JOIN employees e ON e.reports_to = m.employee_id LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.support_rep_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY m.employee_id, m.first_name, m.last_name ORDER BY customer_count DESC, m.employee_id

question: Show each billing country's invoice revenue in separate columns for 2011 and 2012.
gold_sql: SELECT billing_country, SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_date >= DATE '2011-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2012-01-01' THEN total ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2011, SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' THEN total ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2012 FROM invoices GROUP BY billing_country ORDER BY billing_country

question: Which billing countries increased invoice revenue from 2011 to 2012?
gold_sql: SELECT billing_country, SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_date >= DATE '2011-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2012-01-01' THEN total ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2011, SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' THEN total ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2012 FROM invoices GROUP BY billing_country HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' THEN total ELSE 0 END) > SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_date >= DATE '2011-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2012-01-01' THEN total ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY billing_country

question: Which month in 2012 had the highest invoice revenue? Return the month and invoice revenue. If months are tied, choose the earliest month.
gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date) AS invoice_month, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM invoices WHERE invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date) ORDER BY revenue DESC, invoice_month LIMIT 1

question: For each genre, return the genre ID and name together with the track ID, track name, and revenue of its highest-revenue track.
gold_sql: WITH track_revenue AS (SELECT g.genre_id, g.name AS genre_name, t.track_id, t.name AS track_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name, t.track_id, t.name), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY genre_id ORDER BY revenue DESC, track_name, track_id) AS rn FROM track_revenue) SELECT genre_id, genre_name, track_id, track_name, revenue FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY genre_name, genre_id

question: For each genre, return the genre ID and name together with the track ID, track name, and duration in milliseconds of its longest catalogue track.
gold_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT g.genre_id, g.name AS genre_name, t.track_id, t.name AS track_name, t.milliseconds, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g.genre_id ORDER BY t.milliseconds DESC, t.track_id) AS rn FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id) SELECT genre_id, genre_name, track_id, track_name, milliseconds FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY genre_name, genre_id

question: For each artist, identify the album with the most tracks. Return artist ID, artist name, album ID, album title, and track count.
gold_sql: WITH album_counts AS (SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name AS artist_name, al.album_id, al.title, COUNT(t.track_id) AS track_count FROM artists ar JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name, al.album_id, al.title), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY artist_id ORDER BY track_count DESC, title, album_id) AS rn FROM album_counts) SELECT artist_id, artist_name, album_id, title, track_count FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY artist_name, artist_id

question: Rank customers within each country by total invoice value using dense ranks. Return country, customer ID, first name, last name, total invoice revenue, and country rank. Order countries alphabetically, then by country rank and customer ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: WITH customer_revenue AS (SELECT c.country, c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COALESCE(SUM(i.total), 0) AS revenue FROM customers c LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.country, c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name) SELECT country, customer_id, first_name, last_name, revenue, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS country_rank FROM customer_revenue ORDER BY country, country_rank, customer_id

question: Show monthly invoice revenue and cumulative revenue over time.
gold_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date) AS invoice_month, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM invoices GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date)) SELECT invoice_month, revenue, SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY invoice_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_revenue FROM monthly ORDER BY invoice_month

question: What percentage of realised revenue did each artist generate? Return artist ID, artist name, revenue, and revenue percentage.
gold_sql: WITH artist_revenue AS (SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM artists ar JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name) SELECT artist_id, name, revenue, 100.0 * revenue / SUM(revenue) OVER () AS revenue_percentage FROM artist_revenue ORDER BY revenue DESC, name, artist_id

question: For each year, how many customers placed more than one order?
gold_sql: WITH customer_year_orders AS (SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) AS invoice_year, customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_id) AS order_count FROM invoices GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date), customer_id) SELECT invoice_year, COUNT(*) AS repeat_customer_count FROM customer_year_orders WHERE order_count > 1 GROUP BY invoice_year ORDER BY invoice_year

question: How many distinct customers purchased each genre? Return genre ID, genre name, and customer count.
gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, COUNT(DISTINCT i.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_id = ii.invoice_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY customer_count DESC, g.name, g.genre_id

question: For each sold track, how many distinct customers purchased it? Return track ID, track name, and customer count.
gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name, COUNT(DISTINCT i.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM tracks t JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_id = ii.invoice_id GROUP BY t.track_id, t.name ORDER BY customer_count DESC, t.name, t.track_id

question: For each genre that has both sold and unsold catalogue tracks, compare their average durations in minutes. Return genre ID, genre name, average duration of sold tracks, and average duration of unsold tracks.
gold_sql: WITH sold_tracks AS (SELECT DISTINCT track_id FROM invoice_items) SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, AVG(CASE WHEN st.track_id IS NOT NULL THEN t.milliseconds / 60000.0 END) AS sold_average_minutes, AVG(CASE WHEN st.track_id IS NULL THEN t.milliseconds / 60000.0 END) AS unsold_average_minutes FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id LEFT JOIN sold_tracks st ON st.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name HAVING COUNT(st.track_id) > 0 AND COUNT(CASE WHEN st.track_id IS NULL THEN 1 END) > 0 ORDER BY g.name, g.genre_id

question: Which customers bought Rock tracks but never bought Jazz tracks? Return customer ID, first name, and last name.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE i.customer_id = c.customer_id AND g.name = 'Rock') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE i.customer_id = c.customer_id AND g.name = 'Jazz') ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name, c.customer_id

question: Among customers billed in the USA during 2012, who had the highest realised line-item revenue? Return customer ID, first name, last name, and realised revenue. If customers are tied, choose by customer ID in ascending order.
gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id WHERE i.billing_country = 'USA' AND i.invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND i.invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.customer_id LIMIT 1

question: Who are our top customers?
clarification_target: Ask whether top means realised revenue, invoice total, order count, or units purchased.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use realised line-item revenue. Return exactly ten rows containing customer ID, first name, last name, and total realised revenue.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON i.invoice_id = ii.invoice_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10

question: Show me the most popular tracks.
clarification_target: Ask whether popularity means units sold, realised revenue, or playlist inclusion.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use units sold and return exactly ten rows containing track ID, track name, and units sold. Order by units sold in descending order, and break ties alphabetically by track name and then by track ID in ascending order.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name, SUM(ii.quantity) AS units_sold FROM tracks t JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY t.track_id, t.name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, t.name, t.track_id LIMIT 10

question: Which artists perform best?
clarification_target: Ask whether performance means realised revenue, units sold, album count, or catalogue track count.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use realised line-item revenue and return exactly ten rows containing artist ID, artist name, and realised revenue. Order by revenue in descending order, and break ties alphabetically by artist name and then by artist ID in ascending order.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM artists ar JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, ar.name, ar.artist_id LIMIT 10

question: What are our biggest markets?
clarification_target: Ask for the market geography and ranking metric, such as billing country by revenue or customer country by customer count.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use invoice billing country as the market and total invoice value as revenue. Return billing country and invoice revenue, ordered by revenue in descending order. Break ties alphabetically by billing country.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT billing_country, SUM(total) AS invoice_revenue FROM invoices GROUP BY billing_country ORDER BY invoice_revenue DESC, billing_country

question: Which genres are doing well?
clarification_target: Ask whether to measure genres by realised revenue, units sold, buyers, or catalogue size.

resolution.scriptedReply: Measure genres by realised line-item revenue across all available years. Return genre ID, genre name, and revenue.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, g.name, g.genre_id

question: How are sales doing lately?
clarification_target: Ask for both the sales metric and the period meant by lately.

resolution.scriptedReply: Show monthly realised line-item revenue during 2013.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', i.invoice_date) AS invoice_month, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id WHERE i.invoice_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND i.invoice_date < DATE '2014-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', i.invoice_date) ORDER BY invoice_month

question: Show recent customer purchases.
clarification_target: Ask for the period meant by recent.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use calendar year 2013 and list the customer, invoice, track, and quantity for each purchase. Return customer ID, first name, last name, invoice ID, invoice date, track ID, track name, and quantity.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, i.invoice_id, i.invoice_date, t.track_id, t.name AS track_name, ii.quantity FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id WHERE i.invoice_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND i.invoice_date < DATE '2014-01-01' ORDER BY i.invoice_date, i.invoice_id, ii.invoice_line_id

question: Compare this year's revenue with last year.
clarification_target: Ask which dataset year should be treated as this year because Chinook is historical.

resolution.scriptedReply: Treat 2013 as this year and compare total invoice value with 2012.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) AS invoice_year, SUM(total) AS invoice_revenue FROM invoices WHERE invoice_date >= DATE '2012-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2014-01-01' GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) ORDER BY invoice_year

question: List the important invoices.
clarification_target: Ask what makes an invoice important, such as total threshold, country, customer, or date.

resolution.scriptedReply: Treat invoices above $20 as important. Return invoice ID, customer ID, invoice date, billing country, and invoice total.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT invoice_id, customer_id, invoice_date, billing_country, total FROM invoices WHERE total > 20 ORDER BY total DESC, invoice_id

question: Show expensive music.
clarification_target: Ask whether music means tracks or albums and what price threshold defines expensive.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use tracks and define expensive as a catalogue price above $1.00. Return track ID, track name, and unit price.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT track_id, name, unit_price FROM tracks WHERE unit_price > 1.00 ORDER BY unit_price DESC, name, track_id

question: Show sales by country.
clarification_target: Ask whether country means invoice billing country or the customer's recorded country.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use invoice billing country and total invoice value.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT billing_country, SUM(total) AS invoice_revenue FROM invoices GROUP BY billing_country ORDER BY invoice_revenue DESC, billing_country

question: How much did each customer spend?
clarification_target: Ask whether spending should use invoice header totals or realised line-item revenue.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use invoice header totals across all available years. Return customer ID, first name, last name, and amount spent.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COALESCE(SUM(i.total), 0) AS amount_spent FROM customers c LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY amount_spent DESC, c.customer_id

question: Which country buys the most Rock?
clarification_target: Ask whether country means billing country or customer country and whether most means units or revenue.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use invoice billing country and compare Rock purchases by units sold. Return the single billing country and Rock units sold with the highest value, breaking ties alphabetically by billing country.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT i.billing_country, SUM(ii.quantity) AS rock_units_sold FROM invoices i JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE g.name = 'Rock' GROUP BY i.billing_country ORDER BY rock_units_sold DESC, i.billing_country LIMIT 1

question: Give me revenue per employee.
clarification_target: Ask whether revenue should be attributed to support representatives through their assigned customers or by another relationship.

resolution.scriptedReply: Attribute realised line-item revenue to support representatives through their assigned customers. Return employee ID, first name, last name, and revenue.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM employees e JOIN customers c ON c.support_rep_id = e.employee_id JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.invoice_id = i.invoice_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name ORDER BY revenue DESC, e.employee_id

question: Show me some long tracks.
clarification_target: Ask for a duration threshold or a requested top-N count.

resolution.scriptedReply: Use a duration threshold of ten minutes and show every matching track. Return track ID, track name, and duration in milliseconds.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT track_id, name, milliseconds FROM tracks WHERE milliseconds > 600000 ORDER BY milliseconds DESC, track_id

question: Which customers order frequently?
clarification_target: Ask for the minimum order count and any time period.

resolution.scriptedReply: Define frequent as at least seven orders across all available years. Return customer ID, first name, last name, and order count.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT i.invoice_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT i.invoice_id) >= 7 ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.customer_id

question: Are Rock sales better than Jazz sales?
clarification_target: Ask whether better means units or revenue and whether a time period applies.

resolution.scriptedReply: Compare Rock and Jazz by realised line-item revenue across all available years.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT g.name AS genre_name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id WHERE g.name IN ('Rock', 'Jazz') GROUP BY g.name ORDER BY g.name

question: Did we improve in 2012?
clarification_target: Ask which metric should improve and which comparison period should be used.

resolution.scriptedReply: Compare total invoice value in 2012 with 2011.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) AS invoice_year, SUM(total) AS invoice_revenue FROM invoices WHERE invoice_date >= DATE '2011-01-01' AND invoice_date < DATE '2013-01-01' GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM invoice_date) ORDER BY invoice_year

question: List customers and employees in Canada with invoices.
clarification_target: Ask whether in Canada modifies customers, employees, invoices, or more than one of them.

resolution.scriptedReply: Canada applies to the customers; list those customers and their invoices. Return customer ID, first name, last name, invoice ID, invoice date, billing country, and invoice total.
resolution.gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, i.invoice_id, i.invoice_date, i.billing_country, i.total FROM customers c JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.country = 'Canada' ORDER BY c.customer_id, i.invoice_date, i.invoice_id

question: Show albums by artists with Rock tracks and sales over $10.
clarification_target: Ask whether the $10 threshold applies per album, per artist, per track, or per invoice.

resolution.scriptedReply: Apply the $10 threshold to each artist's total realised revenue across all tracks, require at least one Rock track, and list all albums by qualifying artists. Return artist ID, artist name, album ID, and album title.
resolution.gold_sql: WITH qualifying_artists AS (SELECT ar.artist_id FROM artists ar JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id JOIN tracks t ON t.album_id = al.album_id LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.track_id = t.track_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN t.genre_id = (SELECT genre_id FROM genres WHERE name = 'Rock') THEN 1 END) > 0 AND COALESCE(SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity), 0) > 10) SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name AS artist_name, al.album_id, al.title AS album_title FROM qualifying_artists qa JOIN artists ar ON ar.artist_id = qa.artist_id JOIN albums al ON al.artist_id = ar.artist_id ORDER BY ar.name, al.title, al.album_id

turns.question: Which genre has the longest average track duration? Return genre ID, genre name, and average duration in minutes. If genres are tied, choose alphabetically by genre name and then by genre ID in ascending order.
turns.gold_sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.name, AVG(t.milliseconds) / 60000.0 AS average_minutes FROM genres g JOIN tracks t ON t.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.name ORDER BY average_minutes DESC, g.name, g.genre_id LIMIT 1

turns.question: Now return the five longest tracks in that genre, including track ID, name, and duration in milliseconds. Order them by duration in descending order, and break ties by track ID in ascending order.
turns.gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name, t.milliseconds FROM tracks t JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE g.name = :previous_genre_name ORDER BY t.milliseconds DESC, t.track_id LIMIT 5

turns.question: Which artist generated the most realised revenue? Return artist ID, artist name, and realised revenue. If artists are tied, choose alphabetically by artist name and then by artist ID in ascending order.
turns.gold_sql: SELECT ar.artist_id, ar.name, SUM(ii.unit_price * ii.quantity) AS revenue FROM invoice_items ii JOIN tracks t ON t.track_id = ii.track_id JOIN albums al ON al.album_id = t.album_id JOIN artists ar ON ar.artist_id = al.artist_id GROUP BY ar.artist_id, ar.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, ar.name, ar.artist_id LIMIT 1

turns.question: Rank the same genres by realised revenue instead. Return genre ID, genre name, and realised revenue, ordered by revenue in descending order. Break ties alphabetically by genre name and then by genre ID in ascending order.

turns.question: Return the ten longest Rock tracks, including track ID, name, and duration in milliseconds. Order them by duration in descending order, and break ties by track ID in ascending order.
turns.gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name, t.milliseconds FROM tracks t JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE g.name = 'Rock' ORDER BY t.milliseconds DESC, t.track_id LIMIT 10

turns.question: Now return only the top three tracks, including track ID, name, and duration in milliseconds. Keep them ordered by duration in descending order, and break ties by track ID in ascending order.
turns.gold_sql: SELECT t.track_id, t.name, t.milliseconds FROM tracks t JOIN genres g ON g.genre_id = t.genre_id WHERE g.name = 'Rock' ORDER BY t.milliseconds DESC, t.track_id LIMIT 3
